subject: tools/issue-triage-selftest-check
thesis: The captured-self-test-run pattern is documented repeatedly for sibling folders in bee-scouts, but nothing I read shows tools/issue-triage-selftest-check, its recorder, or a committed capture, so the step's premise rests on an unverified folder; the repo's commit stream in the last 30 days reads as maintenance traffic rather than shipping work.

claims.label: UNKNOWN

claims.label: FACT

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Issue #159 states it could not confirm from the index or snippets what SELFTEST_OUTPUT.md currently contains, nor whether the folder holds an expected-output file by any name.

risks: No page I read shows tools/issue-triage-selftest-check, its record_selftest.py, its self_test.py, or any SELFTEST_OUTPUT.md, so the subject's existence and contents are unverified.

The repository's recent commit volume is dominated by health-check messages, and the service check classifies none of the last 30 days' raw commits as real work, so activity is hard to read as building.
The sibling proposals are labelled 'bee-proposal' and 'A person decides; an agent never merges anything', so proposals existing does not mean they were adopted or that the output files exist.
Capturing a run verbatim only proves the tool behaved the way it printed on that machine at that moment; page texts give no evidence of a re-run or independent verification.
Issue #159 itself says it could not confirm what SELFTEST_OUTPUT.md currently contains or whether an expected-output file exists, which is the same gap for the folder in this step.
unknowns: Whether HivemindOS-Agents/bee-scouts is still shipping: None of its commits in the last 30 days is real work.
